active_family: 310 learned center plus level residual flow
current_bottleneck: The learned-center residual family now shows a clean coordinate tradeoff. Transition residuals preserve cross-cell dependence and jump geometry better; level residuals preserve calibration, unconditional shape, and long-horizon anchoring better. The next question is whether one model can keep the level-path target while also seeing implied daily changes explicitly.
last_result_summary: 309a versus 310a clarified that the family is not incoherent. 309a was better on corr ratio, rank ratio, active MR cells, and local jump/move geometry; 310a was better on calibration, kurtosis/skewness, cointegration, level KS, and median bias. The evidence points to missing local move-state exposure inside the level-residual formulation rather than a need for a new paradigm.
next_step_recommendation: Implement 311a: keep the learned deterministic center and the level-residual path target from 310a, but expose implied total daily transitions as an extra state channel to the vanilla joint flow. This is the smallest clean test of whether the 309a/310a tradeoff can be reconciled without adding shell machinery or another latent hierarchy.
